course.description: A hands-on guide to building and deploying a live expense tracker dashboard using Google Apps Script — no new vendors, no IT tickets, no cost. Includes complete Code.gs and HTML you can copy and run today.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Build Your First Google Apps Script Finance Dashboard.

lessons.content:
## Why Google Apps Script?

If your company uses Google Workspace, you already have a full application platform — frontend, backend, database, authentication, and deployment — sitting inside your account. No new vendors. No IT tickets. No procurement. No cost.

Google Apps Script lets you build and deploy internal tools that are already behind your company's SSO, already compliant, and already approved.

This guide walks you through building a **live expense tracker dashboard** from scratch. By the end, you'll have a working web app your team can use today.

---

## Step 1: Create the Spreadsheet

1. Go to [Google Sheets](https://sheets.google.com) and create a new spreadsheet
2. Rename it to **"Expense Tracker"**
3. Rename the first tab (bottom of screen) to **`Expenses`**

### Set Up the Columns

In row 1 of the `Expenses` tab, add these headers:

| A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Date** | **Category** | **Amount** | **Description** |

### Add Some Sample Data

Add 5–10 rows of sample expenses so you have data to work with:

| Date | Category | Amount | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 2026-05-01 | Software | 49.99 | Figma subscription |
| 2026-05-03 | Travel | 234.50 | Flight to Chicago |
| 2026-05-05 | Office Supplies | 67.20 | Printer paper and toner |
| 2026-05-10 | Software | 20.00 | Notion team plan |
| 2026-05-12 | Meals | 85.00 | Client lunch |
| 2026-05-15 | Travel | 150.00 | Uber rides (May) |
| 2026-05-18 | Software | 99.00 | Slack annual |
| 2026-05-20 | Office Supplies | 42.30 | Standing desk mat |

### Create a Config Tab

1. Click the **+** at the bottom to add a new tab
2. Name it **`Config`**
3. In the Config tab, add your expense categories:

| A |
|---|
| **Category** |
| Software |
| Travel |
| Office Supplies |
| Meals |
| Professional Development |
| Equipment |
| Other |

This Config tab will drive the dropdown in your dashboard's add-expense form. When you need a new category, just add a row here — no code changes needed.

---

**What you have now:** A Google Sheet with expense data and a config tab. This is your database. Next, we'll write the backend code that reads and writes to it.

lessons.content:
## Deploy Your Dashboard

1. In the Apps Script editor, click the blue **Deploy** button (top right)
2. Select **New deployment**
3. Click the gear icon next to "Select type" → choose **Web app**
4. Fill in the settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Description** | v1 — Expense Tracker Dashboard |
| **Execute as** | Me |
| **Who has access** | Anyone within [your organization] |

5. Click **Deploy**
6. Google will ask you to **authorize** the app — click through the permissions. This is the app asking to read/write your spreadsheet. It only has access to *this* spreadsheet.
7. Copy the **Web app URL** — this is your dashboard's live link.

---

## Test It

1. Open the URL in a new browser tab
2. You should see your dashboard with the sample data loaded
3. Add an expense through the form
4. Go back to your Google Sheet — the new row is there
5. Share the URL with a colleague — if they're in your organization, it just works. No login screen, no setup.

---

## Updating Your App

When you make code changes:

1. Click **Deploy → Manage deployments**
2. Click the **pencil icon** on your existing deployment
3. Change the version dropdown to **New version**
4. Click **Deploy**

Your URL stays the same. Users see the update immediately.

---

## Access Control Options

| "Who has access" setting | What it means |
|--------------------------|---------------|
| **Only myself** | Just you — good for testing |
| **Anyone within [org]** | Anyone with a company Google account — the sweet spot for internal tools |
| **Anyone** | Public internet — use with caution |

For most finance dashboards, **"Anyone within [org]"** is the right choice. Everyone on your team can access it, but nobody outside your company can.

---

## What About Security?

This is the key insight: **there's nothing new to approve.**

- The app runs on Google's infrastructure (same as Sheets, Docs, Drive)
- Authentication is handled by your existing Google SSO
- Data stays in your Google Sheet — same compliance boundary as any other Sheet
- Your IT admin can see and manage all Apps Script deployments in the Admin Console
- No third-party vendor. No external API calls. No data leaving Google.

Your company already reviewed and approved Google Workspace. This dashboard runs *inside* that approval.

---

**You now have a live, deployed web app.** Next: how to customize it and make it your own.
